//: Each case names the rule it exists to protect. Delete that rule from the prompt, run this, and the cases that fail tell you what the rule was buying. A case with no `guards` is a case nobody can act on.

global.//: Applied to every case that comes back with SQL. These are the mistakes that are always wrong, whatever was asked.

absentPattern.//: The output contract says every literal the question supplies is bound as a parameter and referenced by name. Nothing tested that until this line, and it tests it on every case at once rather than one - which makes it the cheapest assertion in the file and the one most likely to catch a trim of the contract block.

cases.guards: Today's date is for relative periods only. A question naming its own month must use that month.
cases.question: what is the cpi in june 2025

cases.guards: Same, for a year rather than a month.
cases.question: what was the average sofr rate in 2023

cases.guards: Term mapping: 'inflation' is YearOverYearPct, a column no question ever names.
cases.question: how much have prices risen over the last year

cases.guards: Term mapping: 'interest rate' is RatePercent in the SOFR view.
cases.question: what is the overnight borrowing rate right now

cases.guards: Term mapping: 'how much was borrowed' is VolumeUsdBillions, and it is in billions.
cases.question: how much was borrowed overnight in march 2025

cases.guards: A window that runs past what is held is still queried, not refused and not shortened.
cases.question: what was the year over year inflation rate for the last 3 months

cases.guards: Two datasets at once is answerable; join at month grain, averaging SOFR up.
cases.question: what is the relation between cpi and sofr for the year 2025

cases.guards: How a series CHANGED needs LAG over an aggregate, and TOP (1) for 'which'.
cases.question: between which months did sofr change the most in 2025

cases.guards: 'When was it highest' takes TOP with ORDER BY rather than returning every period.
cases.question: which month had the highest cpi in 2024

cases.guards: M13 is the annual average, not a thirteenth month. Guessing a code returns nothing.
cases.question: what was the annual average cpi for 2022

cases.guards: Term mapping: 'did anything fail' is the collection health view.
cases.question: did any sources fail to collect this week

cases.guards: 'Latest' for one headline figure has its own view.
cases.question: what is the most recent cpi figure you have

cases.guards: A range is half-open; BETWEEN with a guessed month-end drops the 31st on daily SOFR.
cases.question: what was the average sofr rate in january 2025

cases.guards: 'Unanswerable' is for subjects these views do not hold — not for windows that come back short.
cases.question: what is the current unemployment rate in the united states

cases.guards: 'What IS cpi' is a definition and must classify, not query. 'What WAS cpi' must not hit this.
cases.question: what is cpi and who publishes it

cases.guards: A follow-up resolves against the prior turn's bound parameters, not its answer.
cases.question: and what about the year before that

history.question: what is the average cpi of 2022
history.sql: SELECT AnnualValue FROM analytics.vw_CpiAnnual WHERE ReferenceYear = @year

cases.guards: The output contract's parameterisation rule. A question naming a month must bind it, not inline it.
cases.question: what was cpi in march 2024

cases.guards: The about_platform arm of the refusal taxonomy in the output contract. Only about_cpi was tested.
cases.question: what data do you have and how often do you collect it

cases.guards: The not_a_data_question arm of the taxonomy. The pleasantry filter catches most of these before the model, but not all.
cases.question: thanks, that helps a lot

cases.guards: 'S01'/'S02' and FirstHalfValue exist. A guessed code returns nothing, which reads as no data.
cases.question: what was the average cpi for the first half of 2024

cases.guards: M13 is the annual average BLS publishes, not a thirteenth month - and not something to reconstruct by averaging twelve rows.
cases.question: what was cpi for the whole of 2023

cases.guards: Every view already filters to the current vintage, so deduplicating revisions is work that can only go wrong.
cases.question: what was cpi in each month of 2024

cases.guards: The revision views and their notes. 'Has it been revised' is the one question the current-vintage views cannot answer.
cases.question: has the june 2025 cpi figure been revised

cases.guards: Weeks are rolling, not calendar. Asked on a Tuesday, a calendar week starts 2026-08-10 and the rolling one starts 2026-08-05.
cases.question: what was the average sofr rate this week

cases.guards: Relative-date resolution against today, for a phrase the temporal block names explicitly.
cases.question: what is the average sofr rate year to date

cases.guards: A referent two turns back, which is also what the history-compaction setting is betting on.
cases.question: and the one before that

history.question: what is the average cpi of 2022
history.sql: SELECT AnnualValue FROM analytics.vw_CpiAnnual WHERE ReferenceYear = @year

history.question: and the year before that
history.sql: SELECT AnnualValue FROM analytics.vw_CpiAnnual WHERE ReferenceYear = @year

cases.guards: 'Carry the reference only'. A follow-up that names its own subject and period completely is a new question.
cases.question: what was the average sofr rate in 2023

history.question: what is the average cpi of 2022
history.sql: SELECT AnnualValue FROM analytics.vw_CpiAnnual WHERE ReferenceYear = @year

cases.guards: A referent that is not in the conversation at all is a refusal, not a guessed period.
cases.question: and what about the year before that
